metadata.name: xargs
metadata.displayName: xargs - Build and execute command lines from standard input
metadata.description: Build and execute command lines from standard input

installation.note: xargs is a built-in command available on all Linux systems by default

overview.summary: The xargs command reads items from standard input and executes a command for each item (or group of items). It's extremely useful for processing lists of files, handling command-line argument limits, and building pipelines where one command's output becomes arguments to another command.
when_to_use: Process lists of files from find or other commands
Process output from other commands as arguments

syntax.description: Read items from stdin, execute COMMAND with those items as arguments. If no COMMAND is specified, defaults to 'echo'.

options.description: Replace REPLACE_STR with input items in command

options.description: Use at most N arguments per command invocation
options.use_case: Limit how many arguments are passed to each command call

options.description: Run up to N processes in parallel
options.use_case: Speed up processing by running multiple commands in parallel

options.description: Input items are separated by null characters (not whitespace)
options.use_case: Handle filenames with spaces or special characters safely
See what commands will be executed before they run
Confirm each command before execution for safety

misconceptions.title: xargs always appends arguments to the end
misconceptions.misconception: xargs can only add arguments at the end of commands
misconceptions.reality: Use -I to place arguments anywhere: ls *.txt | xargs -I {} mv {} backup/ places {} in the middle.
misconceptions.tip: Use -I REPLACE_STR to place input items at specific positions in commands

misconceptions.title: xargs handles spaces automatically
misconceptions.misconception: xargs automatically handles filenames with spaces
misconceptions.reality: xargs splits on whitespace by default. Use find -print0 | xargs -0 for safe handling of spaces.
misconceptions.tip: Always use -print0 with find and -0 with xargs when filenames might have spaces

common_pitfalls.description: Default xargs splits on spaces, so 'file name.txt' becomes two arguments
common_pitfalls.solution: Use find -print0 | xargs -0 for null-separated input that handles spaces correctly

common_pitfalls.description: Some commands have limits on number of arguments (often 128KB total)
common_pitfalls.solution: Use -n to limit arguments per invocation, or -s to limit total size

common_pitfalls.description: xargs rm can be dangerous if input contains unexpected files
common_pitfalls.solution: Use -t to preview commands, or -p to confirm each command before execution

best_practices: Always use find -print0 | xargs -0 when filenames might have spaces
Use -t to preview commands before execution
Use -p for interactive confirmation when operations are destructive
Use -I {} for precise argument placement in commands
Use -P for parallel processing to speed up batch operations
performance_tips: Use -P for parallel processing to utilize multiple CPU cores
xargs is more efficient than calling commands in loops
Batch operations with xargs are faster than individual command calls
Use -n to optimize argument counts for specific commands

additional_notes.default_command: If no command is specified, xargs defaults to 'echo'
additional_notes.argument_limits: Commands have argument size limits (often 128KB) - xargs handles this automatically
additional_notes.null_separation: The -print0/-0 combination is the safest way to handle arbitrary filenames
